summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, and peripheral artery disease was admitted for management of non-healing ulcers on his right foot. He underwent balloon angioplasty of the right anterior tibial artery to improve blood flow, which was successful as evidenced by the return of a palpable dorsalis pedis pulse. The procedure used minimal contrast to protect kidney function, and his renal values remained stable. He was started on clopidogrel for 30 days and advised to hold chlorthalidone until nephrology follow-up. He recovered well, with stable vital signs and pain control, and was discharged home with instructions for wound care, activity restrictions, and follow-up appointments with nephrology and vascular surgery.
